description:
Implements bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads). This is importer work: follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md exactly (read it first, and docs/rules-pack-compiler.md for technique), plus AGENTS.md "Deterministic rules-pack importer work". The SRD freeze guard is intentionally dormant: do NOT touch docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json hashes and do not add thaw notes.

DEFECT: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts (~line 366) emits action:use-an-object effects[].ordinaryInteractionRuleRef = 'rule:interacting-with-objects'. That record is the ENVIRONMENT passage (levers, portcullis, GM-set Strength DC). The relationship declaration (recordRelationshipDeclarations.ts ~186, relation governing-rule) says: "Use an Object names the rule for the free object interaction it is distinguished from."

SUPERVISOR DECISION on the target: 'rule:other-activity-on-your-turn'. Its source text states the rule: "You can also interact with one object or feature of the environment for free, during either your move or your action." Use an Object's own text ("You normally interact with an object while doing something else ... also useful when you want to interact with more than one object on your turn") is distinguished from exactly that one-free-interaction rule. 'rule:interacting-with-objects-around-you' (the bead's earlier suggestion) is only the list of examples and does not state the free-interaction rule; record that comparison as the source evidence in the projection test/comment. Before changing, print all three passages from the committed pack and confirm this reading; if the source contradicts it, choose the passage that states the free-interaction rule and record why in your bd notes.

WORK:
1. Change the projection to emit 'rule:other-activity-on-your-turn'. Do not hand-edit records.json; regenerate through the importer workflow the protocol names (find the generate/verify scripts in package.json / packages/core/package.json and the protocol; the committed pack must match regenerated output exactly, including any .generated ledgers the regeneration rewrites).
2. Review the generated diff: the only intended record change is action:use-an-object's ordinaryInteractionRuleRef (plus derived artifacts that legitimately carry it, e.g. record-relationships.json, source/region ledgers if they reference it). Explain every changed file in your bd notes; stop and investigate unexpected churn.
3. Sibling check (bead text): every action ruleRef / ordinaryInteractionRuleRef emitted by mechanicsProjections.ts (PR #582 lineage) — print each action's source text beside its target rule's text and confirm the target is the governing passage, not a name-alike. Fix any other mismatch the same way, with source evidence; report the full sibling table in bd notes.
4. Regression evidence: extend the existing action projection test (find it under packages/core/test/importers/ or the committed-pack relationship tests) with an assertion that action:use-an-object's ordinaryInteractionRuleRef is 'rule:other-activity-on-your-turn' AND that the target record's text contains the free-interaction clause ("interact with one object or feature of the environment for free"), so a name-alike retarget fails. Do not weaken any existing expectation.
5. Check whether rule-awareness/discovery tests (packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts, discovery tests, tools.test.ts lookup_rules envelope cases) pin the old target; update only with source-backed reasoning.

OUT OF SCOPE: any engine/runtime code; other importer classes.
